alt: A 6 by 6 grid with a square query marked. Four blocks whose side is the largest power of two that fits are laid over the four corners of the square, one at a time. Cells covered by one block are marked, cells covered by two or more blocks are marked differently, and the answer is the maximum of the four block maximums.

steps.caption: A query for the maximum of the square of side 5 whose top-left corner is row 0, column 0.
The largest power of two that fits in 5 is 2^2 = 4, since (5).bit_length() - 1 = 2. Blocks of side 4 will cover the square.
The top-left block, table level 2 at (0, 0), covers rows 0 to 3 and columns 0 to 3. Its maximum is 35.
The top-right block, table level 2 at (0, 1), covers rows 0 to 3 and columns 1 to 4. Its maximum is 36.
The bottom-left block, table level 2 at (1, 0), covers rows 1 to 4 and columns 0 to 3. Its maximum is 34.
The bottom-right block, table level 2 at (1, 1), covers rows 1 to 4 and columns 1 to 4. Its maximum is 36.
The answer is max(35, 36, 34, 36) = 36. Cells shared by two or more blocks were read more than once, which does not change a maximum.
A query for the maximum of the square of side 3 whose top-left corner is row 1, column 1.
The largest power of two that fits in 3 is 2^1 = 2, since (3).bit_length() - 1 = 1. Blocks of side 2 will cover the square.
The top-left block, table level 1 at (1, 1), covers rows 1 to 2 and columns 1 to 2. Its maximum is 34.
The top-right block, table level 1 at (1, 2), covers rows 1 to 2 and columns 2 to 3. Its maximum is 34.
The bottom-left block, table level 1 at (2, 1), covers rows 2 to 3 and columns 1 to 2. Its maximum is 27.
The bottom-right block, table level 1 at (2, 2), covers rows 2 to 3 and columns 2 to 3. Its maximum is 33.
The answer is max(34, 34, 27, 33) = 34. Cells shared by two or more blocks were read more than once, which does not change a maximum.
A query for the maximum of the square of side 4 whose top-left corner is row 2, column 0.
The largest power of two that fits in 4 is 2^2 = 4, since (4).bit_length() - 1 = 2. Blocks of side 4 will cover the square.
The top-left block, table level 2 at (2, 0), covers rows 2 to 5 and columns 0 to 3. Its maximum is 33. With side a power of two, this is the whole square, and the other three are the same block.
One lookup gives the answer, 33. Four lookups would read the same cell four times.
